prompt_preview:
Read-only planning specialist. Give one actionable plan, risks and a bounded falsifying test; do not edit files.
Read-only bounded planning: repository /home/rb/worktrees/borsuk-prod-ready-v9 exact HEAD 0e86ce56eac3904c43852f6ba931298f6387c75a. Operator goal cold generic Rust S3 ANN latency/QPS at same recall; SIMD/parallelism requested. No edits, native/Cargo/data/network/jobs/children/reviews. Source via git show exact HEAD, avoid stale index/worktree. Evidence committed docs/research/performance-architecture-20260930/cohere1024/cold-membership-discovery/cold-abba-a0001/closed/README.md and cold CPU-profile directory (find only this docs subtree); page-auth-backend/receipt-repair-a0002/closed/README.md: valid SHA alternate backend REJECT saved5.26%<20%, source unintegrated. CPU sample shares twoBit score13.65%, SQ8 score13.43%, SHA34.65%; SQ8 already8/4/2/1 row-batches, do not repeat as new. PreparedTwoBit::score in rotated_two_bit.rs301+ validates recordlen/scale/inverse then sequential f64 table sum and exact final arithmetic. plan_two_bit_source_walks two_bit_generation.rs613+ scores each32-row unit using FnMut record callback; plane/store/HTTP may have additional callers. Find all actual hot callers before recommendation. Compare smallest across-independent-row batching (preserve each sequential accumulation), explicit x86 SIMD/gathers with generic scalar fallback, versus next SQ8 CPU change. Preserve exact IDs/scorebits/tie/error/callback order/auth/get/bytes/cache/memory and generic dimensions including padded tails; no FMA/reassociation or dataset specialization. Is exact score-bit parity feasible given Rust .sum folding/codegen? Do not assume vectorization benefit; inspect existing assembly proof if available metadata only, no broad cache scans. Return ONE concrete intervention, exact owned files/callsite, risks (including stateful callback first-error semantics), source-only implementation boundary, tiny independent oracle and a fast remote release primitive falsifier/resource/preregistered screen before real cold ABBA. No custom framework/new dependencies/Python product/controller. Distinguish a recommendation from measured gain. Keep output concise, evidence-rich.

active_goal.objective: Ship a production-ready, self-contained Rust BORSUK ANN library on S3/blob storage that beats BOTH S3 Vectors and Turbopuffer at equal or better recall on matched end-to-end p90/p95 latency and throughput per total dollar. This is a product goal, not a report. Support incremental insert/update/delete, authenticated generation-pinned publication and reads, bounded RAM/cache/concurrency, restart/recovery, and in-process automatic or callable compaction/GC; require no separate maintenance instance. Preserve current V282 on-demand SQ8 work and live jobs; do not duplicate consultations or paid runs. Opus 5.5 estimates the current PQ64 plus f32 summary/unit router at 184 resident bytes per row, or about 18.4 GB at 100M D768, before old-generation pinning. This is a projection, not a measurement. Reconcile prior V139/V146/V149/V150 centroid-page failures and the completed Fable review before choosing any new arm; do not repeat a known failure. Predeclare a feasible 100M RAM, GET, byte, p90 and cost envelope. Prefer a small resident router and one parallel S3 fetch wave, but choose memory versus quality from a measured Pareto curve, not an arbitrary 2 GB cap. Candidate design: balanced hierarchical semantic cells with physical locality and boundary coverage; scan small SQ8 leaves, split skewed/diffuse leaves, use local compressed indexing only where measured cell-specific gains justify it. Avoid S3 graph pointer chasing and full-vector/full-graph hydration. First run the cheapest distinct paired 100k D768 cosine k100 falsifier on ReLAION and CoHere against unchanged V282, decomposing exact-GT loss into router, selected-cell coverage, local index and SQ8 quantization and counting GETs, bytes, RAM and route CPU. Use V282 98% mean recall@100, p05 95, 32 GET and 16 MiB caps unless a redesign is predeclared; kill weak arms early. Freeze a winner for fresh 1M cold HTTP, then 10M and 100M scale. Measure p50/p90/p95/p99, QPS, RSS including generation swap, physical S3 requests/bytes/retries/errors, build and incremental-maintenance cost, total lifecycle cost and failure recovery. Compare competitors on identical corpus, query split, metric, k, filters, cache state, region and concurrency; if only published targets are available, cite date/configuration and label mismatches, never claim a measured win. When a gate fails, redesign routing, layout, quantization or fetch schedule with one causal change per experiment. Unreleased formats need no backward compatibility. Push code, tests, receipts and a concise decision table to BORSUK main. Within 24 hours deliver one substantive object-native library increment and a falsifiable next gate, then continue until the product works.
active_goal.note: re-apply delivery failed; prior goal state restored

partial_result:
**Recommend one bounded intervention: AVX2 gathers within a single two-bit record, preserving the ordered scalar reduction.** This is a candidate to falsify, not a measured gain. All repository inspection used frozen commit `0e86ce56eac3904c43852f6ba931298f6387c75a`.

The [closed profile](/home/rb/worktrees/borsuk-prod-ready-v9/docs/research/performance-architecture-20260930/cohere1024/cold-cpu-profile/profile-a0001/closed/README.md) attributes 13.65% self CPU to two-bit scoring and 13.43% to SQ8 scoring. [SHA backend evidence](/home/rb/worktrees/borsuk-prod-ready-v9/docs/research/performance-architecture-20260930/cohere1024/cold-page-auth-backend/receipt-repair-a0002/closed/README.md) preserves the valid rejection: 5.2563% saving below 20%; candidate unintegrated. Existing assembly metadata proves SHA instructions, but provides no scoring-kernel proof.

The alternatives compare as follows:

| Candidate | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Four independent rows, sequential accumulation per row | Better opportunity to hide accumulation latency, but prefetching through `FnMut` can invoke later callbacks before an earlier scoring error. Preserving that contract requires a separate internal path. |
| Four lookup gathers within one row | Smallest shared intervention; leaves callbacks, validation order and row-at-a-time completion intact. |
| Next SQ8 change | SQ8 already uses 8/4/2/1 row batches at `exact_sq8_nominee.rs:112–168`. Explicit SIMD would need fresh codegen evidence; batching is not new work. |

1. **Implementation boundary.** Change only [PreparedTwoBit::score](/home/rb/worktrees/borsuk-prod-ready-v9/crates/borsuk/src/rotated_two_bit.rs:301), its inline tests, and one ignored release primitive-screen test. After existing record/scalar validation, runtime-dispatch an x86 AVX2 lookup helper. Gather four successive byte-table entries using a tile-relative base and indices `slot * 256 + word`, avoiding dimension-dependent signed-index overflow. Feed the four values into the original ordered `.sum::<f64>()`; handle remaining bytes scalarly. Keep the original scalar fallback and final arithmetic. No horizontal reduction, chunk sums, reassociation, FMA, new dependencies, configuration, format changes or table allocation.

2. **Actual caller reach.** The cold path reaches `score` through [plan_two_bit_source_walks](/home/rb/worktrees/borsuk-prod-ready-v9/crates/borsuk/src/two_bit_generation.rs:637), private `plan_walks:1823`, resident plane access at `1580`, and authenticated fetched-range access at `1730`. The HTTP example calls this generation’s search API; `two_bit_store.rs` has no separate direct scoring call. Other direct callers include hierarchy validation at `hierarchical_semantic_cells.rs:810`, hierarchy searches at `2093/3196`, and nomination binaries at `two_bit_union_nomination.rs:170`, `two_bit_walk_nomination.rs:218`, `v295_rust_two_bit_route.rs:90`, and `v296_two_bit_validation_plans.rs:54`. They inherit the shared change without caller edits.

3. **Parity oracle.** Exact score-bit parity is feasible, but Rust `.sum()` syntax alone is insufficient proof after changing its input iterator. Retain an independent copy of the frozen scalar expression, including reduction initialization and final operation order. Compare `Result` and `to_bits()` against forced scalar and AVX2 paths in debug/release. Cover cancellation, signed zero, all byte values, malformed lengths/scalars, nonfinite results, and dimensions `1,5,255,256,257,768,1024,1025`. Add a stateful planner callback test recording the exact invocation prefix through the first missing or invalid row. Inspect release assembly for ordered additions and absence of FMA/reassociation. Existing tolerance-based score tests are insufficient.

4. **Fast remote falsifier.** After source-bound real-input admission and a separate disposable canary, preregister a same-executable scalar/AVX2 primitive screen on one bounded Spot host: CPU1, 512 MiB, swap0, pids256, measured phase ≤120 seconds. Use fixed 32-row panels, black-box outputs, fixed repetitions and counterbalanced order; exclude preparation from timing. Proposed gate: zero parity/refusal differences, ≥20% median scoring-CPU saving in both orderings, and no >5% regression on other registered geometries. Preserve scratch/resource accounting; no cache or concurrency changes. Setup failures are INVALID. Sync terminal receipts, discard interrupted cells, and terminate compute immediately.

5. **Only then qualify cold ABBA.** Compile affected targets, pass required workspace Clippy and complete test compilation, then freeze source/binary/configuration. Require full 1,000-query parity of ordered IDs, score bits, recall, ties, traces, authentication, GETs and bytes. Preregister fresh cold ABBA with CPU1, width32 and application caches off; use ≥5% p90/p95 improvement in both pairs and QPS nonregression as the new arm’s acceptance screen.

Skipped edits, execution, network, jobs and reviews. Main risk: gathers may cost more than scalar loads, while preserving ordered accumulation leaves its dependency chain intact.
